correctness.rationale: The theorem covers all integer 1<=p<=q and all h>=0 and distinguishes K_2, stars and two nonsingleton classes. Exact orthogonal Laplacian projectors give cross, within-class and diagonal formulas. The RKL2 Legendre representation bounds r in [1/6,1] over [0,5], and r strictly decreases for t>=5; the factored within-small-class offdiagonal is first to turn negative for p>=2. For stars the hub root lies between 5 and 45/8, strictly before any leaf-pair sign loss; all other entries are nonnegative until then. K_2 reduces to scalar r. The eigenvalue p+q yields the exact 2-norm stability threshold. A standard-library-only rational verifier replayed from this package passed 52755 finite assertions. These calculations support but do not replace the analytic all-size proof; independent audit is not performed.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparison with Tan–Aslam–Bertozzi 2026 and 2025 found maximum-principle claims for specified one-dimensional finite-difference grid heat problems, not complete bipartite graph Laplacians. Two closely relevant publicly available mathematical findings were read in full: the three-state RKL2 birth-chain positivity theorem uses a nonsymmetric nilpotent-style generator and gives disconnected windows, while the complete multipartite RK-Taylor study uses third-order coefficient 1/6 rather than the RKL2 1/15. Neither statement implies the exact biclique/star three-case classification. Targeted published-finding corpus queries and web searches did not identify an equivalent or dominating theorem. Priority risk remains for nonindexed specialist sources.
residual_risks: The original 2014 RKL2 paper was available only as an abstract in the inspected material; its full text has not been checked. Method definition and general stability are prior art.
Unindexed publications or theses on positivity of stabilized RK polynomials on complete bipartite networks could establish equivalent sharp formulas.
The result is mathematically same-model reviewed, not independently audited; search nonmatches do not establish absolute historical priority.

value.rationale: A recent RKL2 maximum-principle study establishes results on fixed one-dimensional grid heat problems and cautions that monotonicity need not extend to two-dimensional structures. A complete sharp positivity threshold over all sizes of the natural complete-bipartite family is a structural benchmark, with different first-failure mechanisms for stars and nonsingleton parts and quantified losses from energy stability. The exact threshold, rather than one negative example or a small gain, can guide step selection and reveal the limits of scalar stability for nonnegative diffusion states. Its restriction to uniform graph weights and endpoint matrices is explicit.
